Here’s the Deck breakdown for the Top 32:

There’s a total of 16 different strategies in the Top 32! Kashtira Decks are leading the numbers with 8 Duelists piloting them, but Bystial Dragon Link Decks aren’t far behind with 5 Duelists relying on them for a YCS victory! Spright Fur Hire and Floowandereeze Decks are trailing with 3 Duelists piloting each of those Deck types, while 2 Duelists are on the Sunavalon Rikka strategy. The remaining types of Decks in the Top 32 each have 1 Duelist representing them, but it’s anyone’s guess which Deck and which Duelist will win! Follow the coverage to find out as the North America Remote Duel YCS continues!
Duelists must keep up to date with the newest cards and strategies. Let’s take a look some trends of what our Top 32 Remote Duelists have been using to get an edge on the competition.
The most striking trend is the huge upsurge in the use of
in Side Decks. Almost every single player has 2-3 copies in the Side Deck. Much like

, Ghost Belle is a powerful tool to shut down a very wide range of strategies, like Branded or Tearlaments. However, it doesn’t do much to some of the most popular Decks like Kashtira, so Ghost Belle is relegated to the Side Deck to ensure it only comes in when useful.
Another card popping up in a large of number of Side Decks is

. Anti-Spell inevitably starts showing up as soon as any Spell Card focused Decks become popular – this time, it’s to slow down Purrely. It’s also great against Decks like Sky Strikers or Floowandereeze, or anything with a heavy focus on Fusion Summons.
With the ability to not only remove a bunch of problem monsters, but also potentially win the game off the massive ATK boost it gets,
is an incredible force to reckon with. It’s typically being played in Side Decks even though it’s powerful in most matchups, because it’s primarily a card you want when going second.
and

These cards continue to be popular after their surge in usage over the last few months. Nothing fancy here; they’re just clean, simple cards that have a variety of uses. From blocking an Extra Deck Summon, to turning off key monster effects, to winning in battle against a weaker DEF stat, the versatility keeps Duelists coming back to these old standbys. Being Quick-Play Spells means they’re also flexible enough to use going first or second.

Are you new to “Remote Duels” for the Yu-Gi-Oh! TRADING CARD GAME or confused about how this weekend’s Remote Duel YCS works? Here’s everything you need to know!

In a Remote Duel for the Yu-Gi-Oh! TRADING CARD GAME, players can compete against one another from anywhere in the world! All they need is a video feed, a stable internet connection, and the ability to communicate with other Remote Duel participants. This weekend’s tournament is taking place in a Discord server, so players will need to create an account with Discord in order to compete.

If you’re competing in a Yu-Gi-Oh! TRADING CARD GAME Remote Duel, you’ll need a camera that points to your field of cards so that your opponent can see it. Everything that’s going on in the Duel is visible on that feed, so it’s just like Dueling in person!

Remote Duels are safe and convenient. Many of them also award incredible prizes similar to those that you can win at official in-person Konami tournaments. This weekend’s Remote Duel YCS, for example, awards prizing that is nearly identical to the prizing awarded at an in-person YCS, including the Ultra Rare
prize card and special
trophy for first place!

If you missed out on competing in this weekend’s Remote Duel YCS, be sure to create your Remote Duel setup so that you can compete in future Yu-Gi-Oh! TRADING CARD GAME Remote Duels. The next big official Remote Duel event will be the Yu-Gi-Oh! Remote Duel Extravaganza on July 29th and July 30th, and you can compete in it from your home!
